verdict.rationale: Stripe's docs recommend restricted API keys (RAKs) specifically for keys given to AI agents. RAK permissions limit what an agent can do in the account, and the seller-catalog docs show per-resource permissions enforced with 403 errors. Shared payment tokens add scoped, expiring, revocable payment grants for agent purchases. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of RAK permission granularity, key expiry and rotation for agents, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: RAKs are the recommended type of key for API keys you give to AI agents.
Stripe recommends always using RAKs instead of unrestricted secret keys, especially when giving a key to an AI agent. Use RAK permissions to limit what an agent can do in your account.
Without this permission, API requests return a `403` error
